learning_outcomes.text: Handle the basic equipment of an electronics laboratory.
Learn the operating principles and constitution of the main electronic measurement equipment and systems.
Know the design and development of instrumentation systems.

syllabus_topics: Uncertainty and noise in instrumental systems
Simulated characterization of an RC network
Basic measurements with multimeter and digital oscilloscope
Digital oscilloscope I: characterization of an RC circuit
Digital oscilloscope II: passive RC filter
Weighing system based on strain gauge
Programming instruments for experimental characterization of a diode

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory practicals assessment (tests, report, and presentation)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 4.5 out of 10 is required in the written theoretical/practical exam (AE1). If this minimum is not achieved, the final grade will be 4.9 if the total score is 4.9 or higher, otherwise it will be the actual score. Attendance to laboratory practicals (AE2) is mandatory to pass; this activity is non-recoverable, but the grade obtained is carried over to the extraordinary call. Monitoring questionnaires (AE3) are also non-recoverable, but their grade is carried over. For the global evaluation, there is a single test comprising a written part (80%), a laboratory part (15%), and a CAD design part (5%).
